headline: Skip duplicates only among sibling choices
statement: Return every distinct subset of nums, which may contain repeated integers. A value can occur in a subset no more often than in nums. Include the empty subset. Output ordering is unrestricted.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Sort the numbers so equal values are together. Build subsets by choosing later positions. At one step, choosing either of two equal values would start the same family of subsets, so try only the first. A later step may still choose another copy to include duplicates in a subset.
approach: Sort nums. Save the current path at every call, including the root.
Try each index from start onward.
Skip a repeated value only when i>start and it equals nums[i-1].
Recurse from i+1 and undo the append.
correctness: Paths use strictly increasing indices, so their occurrence counts are legal. The sibling skip chooses only the first occurrence for each next value. Every desired multiset follows a canonical path that takes consecutive equal occurrences at successive depths, giving exactly one path per subset.
bruteForce: Generate every index subset in O(n*2^n) time and remove duplicates afterward.

complexity.explanation: The distinct-input case has 2^n subsets and up to n values per saved copy; duplicates reduce the output.

pitfalls: Use i>start, not i>0, when skipping duplicates.
Save every path, not just full-length leaves.
The empty subset belongs in the result.
